opening.argument: The presentation solicits paid participation in mining pools while promoting recurring income. Viewers are told to purchase computing power, enter the mines based on their comfort level, and expect payouts from Bitcoin mined every day. The displayed plan lists $500, $1,000, and $2,000 shares, connects proceeds to automatic purchases of additional shares, and describes a 1,000-day duration. The opportunity also requires a $99 membership payment and registration through a referring person, with the speaker identifying a referral network and urging viewers to form teams. The compensation plan ties sponsored purchasers to level-up bonuses on their purchases and the purchases of further sponsored participants. Although the speaker cautions against borrowing and denies that the arrangement is a Ponzi, those qualifications do not undo the paid entry, recruitment-linked compensation, or claims that an ordinary participant can make money every day.
